decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the federal funds rate unchanged at 0 to 1/4 percent while formally concluding its asset purchase program.

changes.quote: Labor market conditions improved somewhat further, with solid job gains and a lower unemployment rate.
changes.explanation: The Committee noted that employment metrics have continued to strengthen with robust job creation.

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation have declined somewhat; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
changes.explanation: Market indicators showed lower near-term inflation compensation while long-term expectations remained steady.

changes.quote: Although inflation in the near term will likely be held down by lower energy prices and other factors, the Committee judges that the likelihood of inflation running persistently below 2 percent has diminished somewhat since early this year.
changes.explanation: Temporary energy price drops are weighing on inflation, but the fear of prolonged low inflation has eased.

changes.quote: The Committee judges that there has been a substantial improvement in the outlook for the labor market since the inception of its current asset purchase program.
changes.explanation: The job market has improved enough to meet the goals set when the bond-buying program began.

changes.quote: Accordingly, the Committee decided to conclude its asset purchase program this month.
changes.explanation: The Fed ended its quantitative easing asset purchases because of the substantial economic progress achieved.

tone_quotes.quote: Labor market conditions improved somewhat further, with solid job gains and a lower unemployment rate.
Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's longer-run objective.
Accordingly, the Committee decided to conclude its asset purchase program this month.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.83% APR costs about $49.29 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.34% and moved +4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.97% would rise by about $6.91 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5.9%, and employers added an average of 238k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.7% over the past year (September 2014); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +6 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.21% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Committee plans to keep interest rates low for a considerable time following the end of its asset purchase program.

citations.detail: To support continued progress toward maximum employment and price stability, the Committee today reaffirmed its view that the current 0 to 1/4 percent target range for the federal funds rate remains appropriate.

validation_notes: Forecast probabilities removed from whats_next (the page shows the live computed forecast).
